title: No runbook for an isolated throwaway blackboxd for live validation
wanted_capability: A documented recipe for spinning up a lightweight, isolated blackboxd instance for live validation (HTTP routes, fleet TUI, dispatch) that does NOT touch the prod daemon (127.0.0.1:7264) or its state, and skips heavy startup indexing/edge-rebuild. The host-setup memory covers the managed prod/dev launchd daemons but not an ad-hoc throwaway for validation; an interactive agent validating route/dispatch/TUI changes currently reverse-engineers the env-var set from src/config.rs each time.
missing_primitive: An isolated-daemon validation runbook: the env knobs (BBOX_PORT, BLACKBOX_CONFIG, BLACKBOX_STATE_DIR, TRANSCRIPT_SEARCH_ROOTS, BLACKBOX_KNOWLEDGE_PATH, BRO_HOME, BLACKBOX_REINDEX_INTERVAL_SECS) + a minimal config.toml + a non-prod port, plus teardown.
fallback_used: Derived the incantation by reading src/config.rs, then ran blackboxd on BBOX_PORT=7299 with an isolated BLACKBOX_STATE_DIR/roots/knowledge/BRO_HOME, a 2-line config.toml, and BLACKBOX_REINDEX_INTERVAL_SECS=86400 to skip indexing; validated /control routes + the fleet TUI against it, then killed it and confirmed 7264 untouched.
